title: Does an automatic multi-camera edit survive the audio-sync errors measured on real recorded clips?
summary: Reruns capture-syncedit with every GCC window computed on 10 real recorded clips (the LibreOffice sound gallery, via capture-realaudio) instead of synthetic audio. 4 cameras, a 120 s Viterbi edit at a random point of a 1 h shoot, clocks uniform in ±40 ppm, a Theil–Sen fit over 12 windows of 2 s, 12 seeds per clip. The synthetic result (no damaged cuts down to −10 dB) does not carry over: the mean share of cuts jumping over one 30 fps frame is 0.34 at 0 dB and 0.64 at −10 dB, and four clips lose 62–97% of cuts at 0 dB, while applause, roll and romans stay at 0 down to −10 dB. Partial whitening (gamma 0.25 instead of PHAT) cuts the 0 dB mean to 0.014 but only to 0.48 at −10 dB. Limits: effects rather than field audio, simulated delay, noise and clocks (±40 ppm is swept, not sourced), event rate and the one-frame criterion assumed, gamma chosen in-sample on the same clips, no viewer test.
lede: does an automatic multi-camera edit survive sync errors measured on real clips? Not as on synthetic audio: 34% of cuts jump over a frame at 0 dB SNR (64% at -10 dB) against none, depending on the clip; partial whitening cuts the 0 dB figure to 1.4%.
